questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells drivers that an island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must keep to the right of it.

questions.question: The most common mistake when backing up is not looking both ways behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The most common backing mistake is not looking both ways behind you. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: Yield means you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest. Take time to stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for conditions. Always obey speed limits and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when no other cars are around.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy night traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other cars are around.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling from a curb. Do not skip this step and form bad driving habits.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: The faster your vehicle is going, the longer it takes to stop when you must react to other drivers' sudden moves.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop for unexpected driver actions.

questions.question: The most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best way to reduce your risk of death or serious injury while driving.

questions.question: A driver ahead of you is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Understand that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by talking to passengers, looking for items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, stay far away from them. A distracted driver is more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
Both the alcohol and drug effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, drinking one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like you drank several drinks.

questions.question: What should you do when you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to make them slow down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is being dangerous around you, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Try to get away from them. Do not look at them and do not make rude gestures.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road where cars are backed up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to your exit.
Stop a police officer and ask them to help you get back.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, use the next one. Do not stop or back up on the highway. Do not cross multiple lanes at the last second to make your exit. Do not cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is always dangerous, especially in turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would when driving in slippery conditions.

questions.question: Cell phones can be a serious distraction while driving.
questions.explanation: While driving, do not use cell phones, computers, or other distracting devices, except to report a crash or emergency. Your full attention must be on the road.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed the same and drive straight.
Swerve side to side to warn traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas slowly. Do not brake until you have control. When safe, brake gently and drive to the nearest safe place to stop.

questions.question: An officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Follow what the officer tells you to do.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the officer tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals, except when a police officer is directing traffic instead.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:
questions.explanation: Unless road conditions require it, driving well below the speed limit is dangerous. A slow driver forces other drivers to take risks while passing.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, should you pull to the right side of the road and let it pass?
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens, pull to the right side of the road immediately and let it pass.

questions.question: What is true about signaling before you turn, change lanes, or pull away from a curb?

options.text: You only need to signal if other cars are nearby.
It is good practice and required by law.
You only need to signal during the move, not before.
You do not need to signal if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good practice and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your turn or lane change well ahead of time. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before you move right or left. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: What is important to remember about trucks on the road?

options.text: They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster downhill than smaller vehicles.
They turn in a smaller space than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: What is true about smoking while driving?

options.text: It does not affect your driving.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This creates dangerous distractions.

questions.question: What should you do to cross a railroad safely?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
Cross very quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When can drivers text while driving?

options.text: If you are a skilled driver.
If you only look away for a moment.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is against the law. You cannot use a cell phone or handheld device to send, read, or write text messages while driving. You can only use a hands-free device for voice calls.

questions.question: What should you do if you see water covering the road?

options.text: Drive through until the water seems too deep.
Drive through because the water is probably shallow.
Turn around and take another route.
Walk into the water to check its depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through standing water on a road. You cannot tell how deep it is or how fast the current moves. Your vehicle could be pushed away or sink.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on a layer of water. Low tire pressure, worn tires, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Is it illegal to leave a child under eight alone in a vehicle if conditions are unsafe?
questions.explanation: Never leave a child under eight alone in a vehicle if there is any risk to their health or safety. A person at least 12 years old must always supervise and watch the child.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train might be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers or ignore the sign.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait for your body to process the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers may keep you awake, but they do not lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive in an area.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed for ideal conditions. You must slow down if conditions require it, such as when the road is slippery or visibility is poor.

questions.question: You should never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: To stay alert on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely to take a nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other cars are doing instead of the crossing guard.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a crossing guard tells you to do so. Always drive safely in school zones.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps prevent road rage.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are extra slippery right after rain starts.
You need more space to stop safely.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it starts raining. Your tires travel on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to prevent your wheels from losing grip.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid during quick turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: You notice a defect that could affect your vehicle's safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have the money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that could affect safe driving must be fixed as soon as possible. Fix it before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of colors on a traffic light?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is always on top and green on the bottom. On a horizontal light, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts can double your chance of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury by more than half. Airbags work best when used with safety belts during a front-end crash. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Drivers can always make U-turns in school zones.
questions.explanation: U-turns in school zones are not allowed unless no children are present, school is not in session, or signs show that school zone rules are not in effect.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means you should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes of traffic going the same way will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: Distracted driving usually:

options.text: Slows your reaction time to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: Since driving has risks, it is smart to keep improving your driving and observation skills.
questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe when drivers think they have nothing left to learn. Always work to improve your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.
